title: Attenuated failover holdoff and tenant latency smoother (hotfix)
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: We observed several tenant-facing incidents where sudden short-lived latency spikes caused aggressive regional failover and tenant quarantine. The result was unnecessary cross-region traffic, KV-cache misses, and higher end-to-end tail latency for surviving requests. This PR introduces a conservative 'attenuated holdoff' for failovers and a tenant-level latency smoother that biases early decisioning away from transient spikes. Goals: 1) avoid premature circuit trips and cross-region failover during brief noisy windows, 2) reduce oscillation between degraded and healthy states, 3) maintain fast recovery for true persistent degradation. High-level changes: - Introduce FailoverHoldoffController with an exponential backoff calibration keyed by tenant+region. The controller delays hard failover decisions for a short, bounded window while collecting a weighted moving average of latency and error rates. - Add TenantLatencySmoother: a moving-average + forgiveness token mechanism that applies a soft dampening to immediate SLO breach signals; it allows a small number of high-latency samples to be forgiven within a sliding window before escalation. - Modify circuit breaker evaluation to consult the holdoff controller and smoother before emitting a hard trip; fallback path still allows immediate trips on explicit fatal signals (quota/KV-failure). - Add metrics and tracing: failover_holdoff{tenant,region,state,remaining_ms}, tenant_smoother{tenant,window_ms,forgiveness_tokens}, plus a debug counter for suppressed_failover_events. - Ops/runbook update with guidance and a short rollback path. Backwards compatibility: These changes default to conservative parameters (short holdoff) and are disabled for tenants with a legacy policy flag. Configuration can be tuned via runtime flags and feature gates. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for smoothing logic and holdoff backoff math. - Integration test simulating transient spikes and asserting no cross-region failovers. - Loaded canary for a small subset of tenants (default 3%) followed by staged rollout to 25% then full. Implementation notes: - Files changed touch the runtime decisioning layer and telemetry registration; changes are intentionally minimal in hot paths. - The holdoff controller stores ephemeral state in local memory sharded by tenant; it is designed to be lightweight and not persisted across restarts. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test added - [x] Metrics and tracing added - [x] Ops runbook updated - [x] Canary rollout plan documented Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag. 2) Deploy to Canary region with 3% tenant exposure for 1 hour while monitoring suppressed_failover_events and cross-region egress. 3) If metrics stable (<5% increase in tail latency, no increase in sustained failovers), ramp to 25% for 6 hours. 4) Full rollout if no regressions. Related: ENG-2140 (slo noise reductions), SRE-1021 (incident SUP-887 follow-up).
commits: a6f2d9f: introduce TenantLatencySmoother with unit tests
b3d5ff1: add FailoverHoldoffController and integrate with circuit evaluation
c7a909e: add metrics, tracing and ops runbook update
review_comments: Evan Morris: Can we quantify the memory and CPU cost of keeping per-tenant holdoff state on high-density nodes? Would prefer a sharded LRU with explicit bounds.
Priya Nair: Addressed by using a small fixed-size shard per core and eviction based on last-seen; added a microbenchmark in unit tests and documented expected bytes per-tenant (approx 120 bytes).
Leila Chen: The smoothing window looks sensible but I worry it may hide true regressions for noisy tenants. Can we emit an alert when tokens are exhausted?
Priya Nair: Added suppressed_failover_events counter and an alert in the ops runbook; tokens exhaustion now emits a high-severity metric so SRE can triage noisy tenants.
Marcus Green: CI flake in integration test on first run (timing-sensitive). Suggest using a retry wrapper or lower wallclock sensitivity.
Priya Nair: Integration test updated to poll for stable condition with a 30s deadline instead of fixed sleep. Re-ran CI and green.
notes_for_sre: Key metrics to watch during canary: suppressed_failover_events, cross_region_egress_bytes, p99_latency(tenant), failover_count(region). Ops runbook outlines quick rollback: flip feature flag off, force local circuit reevaluation, and rollback deployment if cross-region egress spikes persist.
release_notes: Hotfix: reduce premature regional failovers by applying a short attenuated holdoff and tenant-level latency smoothing. Default conservative params; feature-gated for controlled rollout.
post_merge_actions: If stable, ramp to 25% per rollout plan
related_incidents: SUP-887: transient latency spike -> aggressive failover (2026-02-08)
changelog_entry: 2026-02-14: Attenuated failover holdoff and tenant smoother added (hotfix) — reduces noisy-triggered failovers and stabilizes tenant experience.
